notes: CBSA's company-name service (GETCOMPY, LINKed by the web front end's GetCompany API with the GETCOMPY copybook's 40-byte COMMAREA, COMPANY-NAME): MOVE 'CICS Bank Sample Application' TO COMPANY-NAME (padded with spaces to 40), then EXEC CICS RETURN. The transaction is CJSA, the CICS Liberty JVM server's default for a web request (the corpus defines none for these programs; the program never reads EIBTRNID). One path, no condition: the scenarios differ only in what the caller leaves in the COMMAREA, which the MOVE replaces whole. The COMMAREA is the program's own DFHCOMMAREA (the copybook starts at level 03). Derived from the CICS Bank Sample Application (CBSA, github.com/cicsdev/cics-banking-sample-application-cbsa; Copyright IBM Corp. 2023), licensed under the Eclipse Public License 2.0: LICENSE here is the corpus's own; NOTICE says what is derived.

scenarios.name: blank-commarea
scenarios.why: the COMMAREA arrives as spaces: COMPANY-NAME becomes the literal, space-padded to 40

scenarios.name: caller-data-replaced
scenarios.why: a COMMAREA full of the caller's bytes: all 40 replaced, the 12 bytes past the literal by spaces

scenarios.name: shorter-caller-name

commarea.COMPANY-NAME: Some Other Bank Name That Is Long

scenarios.why: a shorter caller name under the literal: no byte of it survives the MOVE

scenarios.name: no-commarea
scenarios.why: the caller passes no COMMAREA (EIBCALEN 0, no DFHCOMMAREA): the program still MOVEs to COMPANY-NAME, never testing EIBCALEN

scenarios.name: eibcalen-zero
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 0 with the COMMAREA record present (X23): the MOVE reaches past the bytes the caller passed

scenarios.name: eibcalen-short
scenarios.why: the caller passed 20 of the 40 bytes: the MOVE writes all 40, past EIBCALEN

scenarios.name: longer-caller-name
scenarios.why: the caller's name is 60 characters for the 40-byte COMPANY-NAME: the stated value overruns the field and the MOVE replaces it whole (no byte of the 20 past the field is kept)

scenarios.name: eibcalen-full
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN equals the record (40 bytes, X23): the COMMAREA is stated exact, so the area is cut to the 40 bytes the caller passed and the MOVE fits exactly

scenarios.name: dto-entry-blank-commarea
scenarios.why: as blank-commarea, but the port gets the typed DTO alone (no link-area bytes): the typed entry (in_) and the DTO it gives back (fill_) are what is compared (#5863)

scenarios.name: dto-entry-caller-data
scenarios.why: as caller-data-replaced, through the typed DTO alone: a caller's 40 bytes read by in_ and replaced whole (#5863)

scenarios.name: link-bytes-tail-caller-name
scenarios.why: the caller passes its COMMAREA as raw bytes (handleLink(request, byte[])) and the area runs 10 bytes past the 40-byte record (X10, #7954): the program replaces the name and must leave the tail as it was; the whole area each side left is compared

scenarios.name: link-bytes-tail-blank-record
scenarios.why: as link-bytes-tail-caller-name over a blank record and a 60-byte tail: EIBCALEN is 100, longer than the DTO, and the bytes past the record go back by reference (X10, #7954)

scenarios.name: link-bytes-tail-one-byte

commarea.COMPANY-NAME: Some Other Bank Name That Is Long

scenarios.why: a one-byte tail, the smallest area past the record (X10, #7954): the boundary of cb.length > record length
